context: Diff the live ruleset state (gh api) against the enforcement script's expectations, update the baseline to the documented post-retirement state only, confirm green via a dispatched run, and reconcile the stale activation TODO.
description:
2026-07-21 adversarial UAT review finding (P2, operational): release-canary.yml has been red for 4 consecutive scheduled runs (2026-07-17..20) on the `ruleset drift` job (step 'Fail if ruleset drift was detected'); the other canary jobs (pypi-latest installability, credential-free non-fast) are green. Probable cause: the 2026-07-18 retirement of the require_code_owner_review ruleset target (docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md) was never reflected in _project/scripts/ruleset_review_enforcement.py's expectations.

Impact: .github/workflows/validate-release-pr.yml:57-66 requires a green canary within RELEASE_CANARY_MAX_AGE_HOURS=48, so EVERY release PR is currently blocked regardless of UAT state. This is the single cheapest release unblocker.

Secondary cleanup while in there: the tracker item [[release-canary-scheduled-activation]] rests on a stale premise (its 2026-07-04 evidence says the default branch is main and the canary is unregistered; the default branch has been develop since 2026-07-08, origin/main no longer exists, and the canary is registered and firing on schedule). Reconcile that item: its remaining live content is exactly this baseline refresh.

anti_patterns.dont: mark the canary 'fixed' from a single green workflow_dispatch
anti_patterns.instead: confirm the next scheduled run is green too
anti_patterns.why: scheduled firing is the behavior that matters; dispatch runs can differ in permissions/context

anti_patterns.dont: silence, skip, or continue-on-error the drift job to force green
anti_patterns.instead: update the baseline to the documented, deliberate ruleset state
anti_patterns.why: the canary is the live detection layer for governance drift; a silenced canary is worse than a red one

anti_patterns.dont: widen the baseline beyond what repo-admin-settings.md records
anti_patterns.instead: any additional delta gets its own admin decision documented first
anti_patterns.why: undocumented widening hides real drift behind the legitimate fix

preserves.behavior: The drift check keeps failing loudly on any UNdocumented ruleset change (no blanket allowlist).
pypi-latest-installability and credential-free-non-fast canary jobs unchanged.

the documented 2026-07-18 ruleset retirement the baseline must match
